intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

selected_hotel.name: Golden Circle & Southern Highlands, Iceland Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the aurora borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover to maximize your viewing experience, often venturing to remote highland locations.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars. Booking the Comfort package includes access to the lagoon, a silica mud mask, and an algae mask for a full rejuvenating experience.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic hot spring sits amid bubbling geysers and steaming vents in a stunning rural landscape, offering a more intimate and local experience.

experiences.name: Skyr Tasting & Icelandic Food Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's culinary scene on a guided food tour sampling traditional Icelandic delicacies including skyr (Icelandic yogurt), lamb soup (kjötsúpa), smoked Arctic char, rye bread baked in geothermal ground, and Brennivín schnapps. Learn about Viking-age food traditions and modern New Nordic cuisine.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike
experiences.description: Trek through the surreal rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains of the Fjallabak Nature Reserve and reward yourself with a soak in the natural geothermal hot spring at Landmannalaugar. The hike offers dramatic lava fields, obsidian rocks, and steaming fumaroles, culminating in a blissful natural hot pool surrounded by mountains.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Golden Circle & Southern Highlands, Iceland Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and recover from travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and take the budget-friendly Flybus (approx. 3,500 ISK) to Reykjavik, then connect via shared shuttle toward the Golden Circle & Southern Highlands accommodation. Check in and settle in.
day_by_day.evening: Orientation walk around the local area near your boutique stay. If skies are clear, step outside after 21:00 for your first northern lights watch — January darkness begins early, giving long viewing windows. Download the Icelandic Met Office aurora app to track KP index.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport or bring snacks from home for the flight.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget meal at Keflavik Airport or a petrol station sandwich en route (approx. 1,500–2,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries picked up at a Bonus or Krónan supermarket on the way — stock up on essentials like oats, bread, eggs, and pasta for the week (budget approx. 5,000–7,000 ISK for 2–3 days of supplies).

day_by_day.notes: January in Iceland means only 4–5 hours of daylight (roughly 11:00–15:30). Temperatures average -1°C to 4°C. Pack layers, waterproofs, and grippy footwear. The long nights are perfect for northern lights hunting every evening of this trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þingvellir National Park (free entry) — walk the Almannagjá gorge, the dramatic rift valley where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Arrive by 11:00 to catch the limited daylight. The park visitor centre is free and provides excellent geological and historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Geysir Geothermal Area (free entry to the field) and watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes, shooting boiling water 20–30 metres into the air. Stroll the surrounding hot spring landscape. Nearby Laugarvatn Fontana geothermal baths offer a budget-friendly soak (approx. 3,200 ISK) using natural hot springs — a great warm-up on a cold January afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gullfoss Waterfall (free entry) for a dramatic dusk or early evening visit — floodlights sometimes illuminate the falls. Return to accommodation and monitor the aurora forecast. If KP index ≥ 3 and skies are clear, head to a dark field away from any light pollution for northern lights viewing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or eggs at the accommodation.
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade sandwich and thermos of hot coffee/tea from the accommodation to eat at Þingvellir — saves significant money versus tourist cafés.
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta with canned tomato sauce and cheese at the accommodation (approx. 500 ISK per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle loop (Þingvellir → Geysir → Gullfoss) is approximately 230 km and very manageable in a day. Roads are generally well-maintained but check road.is for conditions every morning — January can bring ice and snow. Fill up your rental car at a Costco or N1 station for the cheapest fuel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Kerið Volcanic Crater (350 ISK entry — one of the cheapest paid attractions in Iceland). Walk the rim of this vivid red and green volcanic caldera with a frozen or partially frozen lake at the bottom in January. The colours are stunning even in winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south toward Seljalandsfoss Waterfall (free entry, parking fee approx. 900 ISK). In January you can walk behind the waterfall — wear full waterproofs as spray freezes on surfaces. Continue 10 minutes east to Skógafoss Waterfall (free entry), another spectacular curtain waterfall. Climb the 370 steps to the top for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the Southern Highlands accommodation. Stop at a local N1 petrol station hot dog stand — an Icelandic institution at approx. 500–600 ISK per hot dog, beloved by locals. Aurora watch from the accommodation grounds or a nearby dark spot if conditions allow.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered yogurt, skyr (Icelandic dairy, buy at Bonus), and fruit.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from accommodation — bread, cheese, and skyr.
meals.dinner: Budget hot dogs at N1 petrol station, then supplement with self-catered soup back at the accommodation.

day_by_day.notes: Seljalandsfoss can be icy in January — microspikes/crampons are highly recommended and can be rented cheaply or purchased at Bonus/Decathlon in Reykjavik. The walk behind the waterfall may be closed if conditions are too dangerous — check on arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Early start to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach near Vík (free entry). Walk the dramatic black volcanic beach, view the basalt column formations (Reynisdrangar sea stacks), and explore Hálsanefshellir cave. WARNING: Never turn your back on the ocean — sneaker waves are deadly here year-round.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Dyrhólaey Promontory (free entry) for panoramic views of the South Coast and black sand beaches from the clifftop. In January, look for wintering seabirds. Continue to the village of Vík for a short explore — visit the iconic hilltop church Víkurkirkja for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation. This stretch of southern Iceland has very low light pollution — one of the best areas in Iceland for northern lights. Set an alarm for 22:00–01:00 and check the aurora forecast. If active, drive 5 minutes from any settlement and look north.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered eggs and toast at accommodation.
meals.lunch: Súpa (soup) at Ströndin Soup Bar in Vík or pack your own — budget soups in Iceland run approx. 1,500–2,000 ISK with bread.
meals.dinner: Self-catered rice and lentil curry at accommodation (approx. 400 ISK per person).

day_by_day.notes: Vík is approximately 70 km from the Golden Circle area — plan for icy road conditions and allow extra driving time. The Reynisfjara beach is free but the car park may charge a small fee. Vík is the southernmost village in Iceland and often has different weather to the interior.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Skaftafell area within Vatnajökull National Park (free entry to the park). Walk the easy Svartifoss trail (approx. 1.5 hours round trip) to see the stunning black basalt column waterfall — the inspiration for Reykjavik's Hallgrímskirkja church architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Book a budget glacier walk on Falljökull or Skaftafellsjökull glacier with a local guide company such as Icelandic Mountain Guides or Local Guide of Vatnajokull (approx. 8,000–10,000 ISK per person for a 2–3 hour introductory walk). This is a must-do experience and guides provide crampons and helmets. Do NOT walk on glaciers without a guide.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back west toward accommodation. Stop at a petrol station for budget dinner supplies. Aurora watch — Skaftafell area is extremely dark and remote, ideal for aurora photography if you have a tripod.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered porridge with honey at accommodation.
meals.lunch: Packed sandwiches and thermos eaten at Skaftafell visitor centre picnic area.
meals.dinner: Self-catered baked potatoes with butter and cheese at accommodation.

day_by_day.notes: Skaftafell is approximately 130 km east of Vík — this is a long driving day. Start early to maximise the limited daylight. The glacier walk is the biggest single expense of the day but is considered unmissable in Iceland. Book in advance online as January spots can fill up.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (free entry to the lagoon viewpoint). Walk along the shore watching icebergs calve from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier and drift through the lagoon. In January the lagoon may be partially frozen, creating surreal ice sculptures. Seals are commonly spotted here year-round.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 200 metres to Diamond Beach (free) — the black sand beach where icebergs wash ashore and glitter like diamonds. Spend time photographing the ice formations as afternoon light (around 14:00–15:30) creates golden tones. Then begin the drive back westward toward the Southern Highlands.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at accommodation by early evening. Rest and prepare for tomorrow. Aurora conditions permitting, do a late-night aurora watch from the accommodation area — the southern highlands are excellent for dark skies.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Jökulsárlón — the café on site is expensive, so bring your own food.
meals.dinner: Self-catered vegetable stew with bread at accommodation.

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 380 km from the Golden Circle area — this and Day 5 work best as a two-day loop staying further east, but can be done from the Southern Highlands with very early starts. Alternatively, consider a budget guesthouse in the Kirkjubæjarklaustur area for nights 5 and 6 to reduce driving fatigue (approx. 8,000–12,000 ISK/night for budget options).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day — sleep in and enjoy a slow morning at the boutique accommodation. Use the time to review photos, plan the second week, and restock groceries. Check the aurora forecast for the coming nights and plan viewing strategies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Haukadalur geothermal area for a self-guided walk among bubbling mud pools, steaming vents, and colourful mineral deposits (free to walk, same area as Geysir). This is a relaxed, low-cost afternoon exploring the geothermal landscape without the crowds of the main Geysir site.
day_by_day.evening: Laugarvatn village evening — visit the small local swimming pool (Laugarvatn Community Pool, approx. 1,000–1,500 ISK) for hot pots, a steam room, and a warm soak. Icelanders use local pools daily and this is a very authentic, affordable experience. Aurora watch on the drive home.

meals.breakfast: Lazy self-catered brunch — scrambled eggs, toast, skyr, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Self-catered soup from leftovers at accommodation.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a budget meal out — Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn offers lamb soup for approx. 2,500–3,000 ISK, or try the Geysir Glima café for budget options.

day_by_day.notes: This rest day is important given the heavy driving of Days 5 and 6. Laugarvatn is a charming small village on the shores of a geothermal lake — the lake itself is naturally warm in places. January is very quiet here, which means more authentic local interactions.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Reykjavik (approx. 1 hour from the Golden Circle area) for a day trip. Walk the main street Laugavegur and explore the colourful old town. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church (exterior free, tower elevator approx. 1,000 ISK for panoramic city views). Visit the Sun Voyager sculpture by the harbour — free and iconic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Harpa Concert Hall (free to enter the lobby and enjoy the architecture). Walk along the old harbour. Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground museum built around actual Viking-age ruins (approx. 2,200 ISK entry) — one of the most affordable and fascinating museums in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation by early evening. If budget allows, the free Thursday evening concerts sometimes held at Harpa are worth checking. Aurora watch on the drive back from Reykjavik — the road between Reykjavik and the Golden Circle passes through very dark areas.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before driving to Reykjavik.
meals.lunch: Reykjavik budget lunch — Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog stand (the most famous hot dog stand in Iceland, approx. 500–600 ISK) near the harbour. A Reykjavik institution.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation — keep Reykjavik food costs minimal by eating out only for lunch.

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavik is expensive for eating out — budget travellers should limit restaurant meals here. The city's Bonus supermarket on Laugavegur is good for stocking up on supplies. Free attractions include all harbour walks, the old town streets, street art, and most church interiors.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þórsmörk (Thor's Valley) — a dramatic glacial valley accessible by super jeep tours in winter (regular cars cannot cross the glacial rivers safely in January). Book a day tour from Reykjavik or the South Coast (approx. 15,000–20,000 ISK) or alternatively explore the Landmannalaugar area if accessible. Check with local operators about January road conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: If Þórsmörk tour continues — enjoy the highland landscapes, glacier views, and birch forest valleys. Alternatively, spend the afternoon at Seljavallalaug — Iceland's oldest swimming pool (free entry, donations welcome), a geothermal pool tucked into a mountain valley, reached by a 15-minute walk. Very few tourists visit in January.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation. Seljavallalaug is a fantastic low-cost hot spring experience. Aurora watch — this area of the south coast has excellent dark skies. Set multiple alarms through the night if the KP index is high.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before the tour.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch for the tour — tour operators rarely include meals at this price point.
meals.dinner: Self-catered noodle stir-fry with vegetables at accommodation.

day_by_day.notes: Seljavallalaug is free but the changing facilities are basic (outdoor, cold). Bring a towel and change quickly. The pool water is geothermally heated and wonderfully warm even in -5°C air temperatures. This is a hidden gem that most tourists miss. The hike in can be icy — wear appropriate footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hekla Volcano viewpoint — drive to the base area of Iceland's most active volcano (free, no hiking on the volcano without guide due to eruption risk). The dramatic landscape of lava fields and the brooding mountain silhouette are spectacular in winter light. Visit the Hekla Centre museum in Leirubakki (approx. 1,500 ISK) for volcanic history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Lava Centre in Hvolsvöllur (approx. 2,500 ISK) — an interactive earthquake and volcano museum that gives excellent context for Iceland's geological activity. Very well designed and educational.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation via the scenic Route 26. Stop at any roadside hot spring or natural pool shown on the Vik to Reykjavik geothermal map — many are free and unmarked. Aurora watch — tonight aim to stay up until at least midnight if the forecast is promising.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats and fruit.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Hekla Centre picnic area.
meals.dinner: Self-catered bean chilli with rice at accommodation.

day_by_day.notes: Route 26 through the interior near Hekla is stunning but check road conditions carefully in January — F-roads (mountain roads) are closed in winter and some routes may be impassable. Stick to paved roads and always check road.is before driving into unfamiliar areas.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated hot springs day — visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir (approx. 3,000 ISK entry). This is one of Iceland's oldest and most affordable geothermal pools, much cheaper than the Blue Lagoon. Soak in the naturally heated pool surrounded by steaming vents and geysers. Arrive early to avoid any groups.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Flúðir village and the surrounding geothermal greenhouse farms (some offer free viewing). Drive to Brúarfoss Waterfall (free entry) — a stunning turquoise waterfall reached by a 4 km round-trip walk. The vivid blue colour of the water is extraordinary and the waterfall is relatively unknown, meaning very few other visitors in January.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation for a final Golden Circle evening. Prepare a celebratory self-catered dinner. Do a dedicated aurora photography session if conditions allow — set up a tripod outside the accommodation and practice long-exposure shots of the northern lights.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before heading to Secret Lagoon.
meals.lunch: Café at the Secret Lagoon offers soup and light meals (approx. 1,500–2,000 ISK) — treat yourself as costs are reasonable here.
meals.dinner: Self-catered celebration dinner — buy a slightly nicer ingredient like local smoked lamb or Icelandic fish from the supermarket (approx. 1,500–2,000 ISK) and cook at accommodation.

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is far better value than the Blue Lagoon (which costs 60,000–100,000+ ISK in peak season). Book the Secret Lagoon online in advance. Brúarfoss trail can be muddy and icy in January — wear waterproof boots. The turquoise colour is caused by glacial minerals and is best seen in daylight.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning aurora debrief and photography review. Pack bags and check out of accommodation. Drive toward Reykjavik, stopping at Þingvellir National Park one final time for a different trail — try the Öxará River walk (free) for a quieter perspective of the rift valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Reykjavik for final afternoon. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) — entry approx. 2,500 ISK, one of the best museums in Iceland covering 1,200 years of history. Alternatively, the Reykjavik Art Museum has rotating free or low-cost exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Reykjavik — walk Laugavegur one last time. Visit a local swimming pool (Sundhöllin or Vesturbæjarlaug, approx. 1,000 ISK) for a final hot pot soak. Buy any last-minute souvenirs from the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends) or Bonus supermarket for edible souvenirs like Icelandic chocolate, licorice, or skyr powder.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast using up remaining accommodation supplies.
meals.lunch: Reykjavik budget lunch — try Hlöllabátar submarine sandwich shop (approx. 1,500–2,000 ISK) or another local chain.
meals.dinner: Final dinner treat — Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) in the old harbour offers legendary lobster soup for approx. 1,800 ISK — one of the best budget meals in Reykjavik.

day_by_day.notes: If staying in Reykjavik tonight, book a budget hostel or guesthouse in advance (Kex Hostel, Oddsson, or Bus Hostel are popular budget options at 5,000–10,000 ISK for a dorm or private room). Keep checking the aurora forecast — Reykjavik's light pollution reduces visibility but driving 20 minutes outside the city gives clear dark skies.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. If time allows before airport transfer, visit the Reykjavik Botanical Garden (Grasagarðurinn) — free entry, peaceful and beautiful even in winter. Alternatively, take a final walk along the Seltjarnarnes peninsula at the western tip of Reykjavik for sea views and birdwatching.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Flybus from BSÍ bus terminal to Keflavik Airport (approx. 3,500 ISK, book online for slight discount). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before departure. Browse the duty-free shop at Keflavik — Icelandic spirits, chocolate, and beauty products are sometimes cheaper here than in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavik International Airport. Reflect on 13 days of northern lights, hot springs, glaciers, and dramatic volcanic landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final Reykjavik breakfast — grab a pastry and coffee from a bakery such as Brauð & Co (approx. 800–1,200 ISK) — famous for their croissants and cinnamon buns.
meals.lunch: Airport café or bring snacks purchased from Reykjavik.
meals.dinner: On the flight home.

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights and car rental): approximately 150,000–200,000 ISK per person (~£900–£1,200 / €1,050–€1,400). Major savings come from self-catering most meals (saves 60–70% vs eating out), using free natural attractions, and choosing local pools over the Blue Lagoon. Car rental in January averages 15,000–25,000 ISK/day — sharing costs with travel companions dramatically reduces the per-person expense. Always buy a local SIM card on arrival for data access to road.is, aurora apps, and maps.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Golden Circle & Southern Highlands, Iceland Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars. Booking the Comfort package includes access to the lagoon, a silica mud mask, and an algae mask for a full rejuvenating experience.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00 — clear customs, collect luggage, and pick up your pre-booked rental car (4WD recommended for January conditions). No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Keflavik toward the Golden Circle area (~1.5–2 hours). En route, stop at the iconic Þingvellir National Park (Thingvellir) to stretch your legs and witness the dramatic rift valley where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. A short walk along Almannagjá gorge is manageable even with luggage in the car.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to your boutique accommodation in the Golden Circle & Southern Highlands area. Freshen up, then head out for your first northern lights watch from the hotel grounds or a nearby dark-sky spot. January offers up to 18+ hours of darkness — ideal for aurora hunting. Download the Vedur Aurora Forecast app to track activity.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport arrivals hall café upon landing.
meals.lunch: Stop at Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn village (~mid-route) — a cozy mid-range spot serving Icelandic lamb soup and fresh trout.
meals.dinner: Dine at your hotel's restaurant or a nearby guesthouse dining room offering traditional Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa) and skyr-based desserts. Budget ~3,500–5,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: January days are very short (~5 hours of daylight). Prioritize safe driving — roads may be icy. Check road.is before every drive. No strenuous activities on Day 1 given travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Geysir Geothermal Area — watch the mighty Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting water 20–40 meters into the air. Explore the surrounding hot spring fields, mud pools, and fumaroles. Allow 1–1.5 hours. The area is free to access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 10 minutes east to Gullfoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's most spectacular two-tiered cascades. Walk the viewing platforms and feel the thundering mist (dress in full waterproofs). Afterward, visit the Gullfoss Visitor Center café for a warm drink.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation and join a guided Northern Lights tour departing from the Golden Circle area (~8,000–12,000 ISK per person). Expert guides drive to optimal dark-sky locations based on real-time aurora forecasts. Photography assistance often included.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at your boutique hotel — skyr with berries, rye bread, smoked salmon, and Icelandic butter.
meals.lunch: Geysir Center Restaurant — hearty lamb burger or fish and chips. Mid-range pricing (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Friðheimar Tomato Farm Restaurant (book ahead) — unique greenhouse dining experience with tomato-based dishes, tomato soup, and fresh bread. ~4,000–6,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Friðheimar requires advance booking — call or book online before your trip. Dress in thermal layers for Gullfoss as wind chill can be severe in January.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Þingvellir National Park for a deeper exploration. Walk the full Almannagjá rift trail and visit Öxará River and Drekkingarhylur (Drowning Pool) — rich in Viking Age history. The park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Laugarvatn Fontana Geothermal Baths on the shores of Lake Laugarvatn — a smaller, less-crowded alternative to the Blue Lagoon. Enjoy multiple geothermal pools, a steam room built over natural hot springs, and a lakeside sauna. Entry ~4,500–5,500 ISK. Geothermal bread baking demonstration available.
day_by_day.evening: Stargaze and northern lights watch from Þingvellir lake shore — one of Iceland's best dark-sky locations. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate and a tripod for long-exposure photography.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs, Icelandic sausage, and fresh coffee.
meals.lunch: Laugarvatn Fontana Café — geothermal rye bread with smoked trout or lamb pâté, baked underground using natural steam. Unique and delicious.
meals.dinner: Lindin Restaurant, Laugarvatn — upscale-casual dining featuring locally sourced Arctic char and reindeer. ~5,000–7,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Laugarvatn Fontana is significantly less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and offers a more authentic local experience. Book in advance for weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip south toward the Haukadalur Valley and Kerið Volcanic Crater — a stunning 3,000-year-old caldera with vivid red and ochre volcanic rock surrounding a serene teal lake. Entry fee ~400 ISK. Walk the full rim (~15 min) and descend to the lake if conditions allow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, dating to 1891. Soak in naturally heated 38–40°C geothermal waters surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser. Entry ~3,200 ISK. Far more intimate than the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation. Self-catered evening — pick up supplies from a local Krónan or Bónus supermarket for a cozy in-room dinner. Monitor aurora forecast and step outside for a spontaneous lights viewing if KP index rises.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from hotel — rye bread sandwiches, skyr cups, and Icelandic chocolate (Nói Síríus brand). Eat at Kerið crater viewpoint.
meals.dinner: Self-catered: Icelandic lamb chops or smoked salmon with potatoes and Icelandic butter, prepared in your accommodation kitchen. ~1,500–2,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Flúðir is a small village — the Secret Lagoon may close early in winter. Confirm hours at secretlagoon.is. Kerið can be icy — wear crampons or ice cleats.

day_by_day.morning: Drive southeast toward Selfoss and then along Route 1 toward Hella. Stop at Urriðafoss Waterfall — Iceland's highest-volume waterfall by water flow, yet relatively unknown. A short hike from the roadside offers dramatic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hekla Volcano viewpoint near Hella — one of Iceland's most active volcanoes with an eerie, cloud-shrouded peak. Stop at the Hekla Center museum in Leirubakki for an educational exhibit on the volcano's eruption history (~1,000 ISK entry).
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the southern highlands atmosphere. Join a snowmobile or super-jeep highland tour if available from a local operator in Hella/Hvolsvöllur area. Alternatively, enjoy a quiet northern lights vigil from your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Árból Guesthouse Restaurant in Selfoss — home-cooked Icelandic meals, daily fish special, and lamb soup. ~2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Hotel Rangá Restaurant near Hella — mid-range dinner with stunning views. Known for northern lights wake-up calls for guests. ~5,000–7,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hotel Rangá is one of Iceland's best northern lights viewing locations. Even if not staying there, dining there is worthwhile. Hekla is active — check volcanic alerts at vedur.is.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's most magical falls where you can walk behind the cascading curtain of water through a cave passage. Extremely icy in January — crampons essential. Entry/parking fee ~750 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 15 minutes along the cliff face to Gljúfrabúi (Hidden Waterfall) — a secret waterfall tucked inside a canyon accessible through a narrow rock crevice. Then drive to Skógafoss Waterfall — a towering 60-meter cascade. Climb the 370 steps to the top for panoramic views of the south coast.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Golden Circle accommodation or stay in the south coast area. Northern lights watch from the black sand beaches near Vík — the lack of light pollution makes this a prime aurora location.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab-and-go pastry from a petrol station bakery.
meals.lunch: Skógar Museum Café near Skógafoss — soup and sandwiches in a warm, historic setting. ~2,000–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík — cozy restaurant with lamb, fish of the day, and vegetarian options. ~4,000–6,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Seljalandsfoss path behind the waterfall may be CLOSED in January due to ice hazard — check locally upon arrival. Skógafoss steps are also icy — use handrails. Vík is ~2.5 hours from the Golden Circle.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach near Vík — dramatic basalt column formations (Reynisdrangar sea stacks), black volcanic sand, and pounding Atlantic waves. WARNING: Sneaker waves are deadly — never turn your back to the ocean. Stay well back from the waterline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Dyrhólaey Peninsula — a volcanic promontory with a natural rock arch and stunning views of the south coast. In January, the lighthouse road may be closed — the viewpoint from below is still spectacular. Watch for Arctic foxes in the lava fields.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Golden Circle base accommodation. Rest and recharge. If aurora forecast is strong (KP 3+), set an alarm for 11 PM–2 AM for peak viewing from the hotel grounds.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Vík accommodation or a local café.
meals.lunch: Black Beach Restaurant, Vík — great views, fresh fish soup, and lamb sandwiches. ~2,500–4,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or prepare a simple meal. Treat yourself to Icelandic Brennivín schnapps (Black Death) as a nightcap — a cultural experience.

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara has claimed lives due to rogue waves. Maintain a minimum 30-meter distance from the water at all times. The drive back to the Golden Circle is ~1.5–2 hours — allow time before dark.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated Blue Lagoon Day — drive to Grindavík (approximately 1.5–2 hours from the Golden Circle). Arrive for your pre-booked morning slot at the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa. Soak in the iconic milky-blue 37–39°C mineral-rich waters. Enjoy silica mud masks, in-water bar service, and steam rooms. Book the Comfort Package (~12,000–16,000 ISK) which includes a towel, one silica mud mask, and one drink.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your Blue Lagoon experience or explore the surrounding lava field landscape. Visit the on-site LAVA Restaurant for a mid-afternoon meal. Afterward, drive the Reykjanes Peninsula's geothermal ridge road — passing steaming vents, sulfur fields, and the Bridge Between Continents (walk between tectonic plates for free).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Golden Circle accommodation. Relaxed evening — soak tired muscles, review photos, and plan remaining days. Light northern lights watch before bed.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: LAVA Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — upscale but worth it for the unique setting. Seafood platter or lamb. ~5,000–8,000 ISK per person.
meals.dinner: Simple self-catered dinner or hotel restaurant. Icelandic lamb stew with flatbread.

day_by_day.notes: CRITICAL: Blue Lagoon requires advance booking — slots sell out weeks ahead. Book at bluelagoon.com before your trip. Bring flip-flops. Silica water can damage hair — apply conditioner before entering. Check Grindavík road access status given recent volcanic activity in the Reykjanes area.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Reykjavik for a city day. Drive ~45 minutes from the Golden Circle. Start at Hallgrímskirkja Church — take the elevator to the tower observation deck for panoramic city views (~1,000 ISK). Explore the colorful streets of the old town around Skólavörðustígur.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Harpa Concert Hall on the waterfront — stunning geometric glass architecture. Walk the old harbor and check out the Sun Voyager sculpture. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn) for an excellent overview of Icelandic history from the Settlement Age (~2,500 ISK entry).
day_by_day.evening: Experience Reykjavik's famous hot pot culture — visit Sundhöll or Vesturbæjarlaug public swimming pools (geothermal hot pots included, ~1,100 ISK entry) where locals gather to socialize. Dinner in the city before driving back.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic food: fermented shark (hákarl), rye bread with smoked lamb, and skyr cake. Authentic and affordable. ~2,000–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Messinn Restaurant, Reykjavik — renowned for its cast-iron pan fish dishes. Excellent value mid-range seafood. ~4,500–6,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavik parking can be tricky on Saturdays — use the Hlemmur or BSÍ parking areas. The drive back to the Golden Circle after dinner is about 45 minutes — plan to leave by 9 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Highland snowmobile or glacier hike experience on Langjökull Glacier — Iceland's second-largest glacier accessible from the Golden Circle area. Into The Glacier tunnel tour (~25,000 ISK) or snowmobile rental (~20,000 ISK per person) available from Húsafell or Gullfoss. Book in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Hraunfossar and Barnafoss Waterfalls near Húsafell — a series of rivulets emerging from beneath a lava field directly into a river, creating a magical curtain-like effect. Free access. Walk the short trail between both falls (~30 min).
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation. Warm up in the hotel hot tub or sauna if available. Northern lights watch — January's long nights offer excellent aurora windows. Set up a camera on a tripod for long-exposure shots.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up well before the glacier activity.
meals.lunch: Húsafell Resort Restaurant or packed lunch from hotel. Warm soup essential after glacier activities.
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant — celebrate the glacier day with a proper Icelandic dinner. Lamb fillet or pan-fried Arctic char. ~4,000–6,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Glacier activities require full winter gear — most operators provide overalls, helmets, and boots. Langjökull road (F-road) requires a 4WD vehicle. Confirm glacier tour availability and road conditions 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Haukadalur geothermal valley beyond Geysir — walk the lesser-visited hot spring fields and mud pots. Visit Bjarnarflag geothermal power station area or drive north toward Lake Þingvallavatn for a peaceful morning lakeside walk in the crisp winter air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Laugarvatn area again for a relaxed afternoon. Try the local swimming pool (sundlaug) — every Icelandic town has one, and they're geothermally heated. Entry ~1,000 ISK. Locals use these daily and it's a wonderful cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated aurora photography evening. Drive to a pre-scouted dark location (lake reflection spots are ideal). Bring a thermos, hand warmers, and a sturdy tripod. Aim for ISO 1600–3200, f/2.8, 10–15 second exposures for aurora shots.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Geysir Center café — quick and convenient. Lamb soup and fresh bread.
meals.dinner: Guesthouse Efstidalur II near Laugarvatn — a working dairy farm with a restaurant serving homemade ice cream and hearty Icelandic farm meals. Unique atmosphere. ~3,500–5,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Efstidalur II is a must-visit — you can often see the cows through a glass wall while dining. The homemade ice cream is exceptional even in winter. Reserve ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Final full exploration day — drive the complete Golden Circle route one more time at a leisurely pace, visiting any spots you may have missed or want to revisit. Stop at the Faxi Waterfall (Vatnsleysufoss) — a quieter, horseshoe-shaped waterfall on the Hvítá River, often visited by local salmon fishermen in summer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kerlingarfjöll geothermal mountain area if road conditions allow (F-road — check accessibility). Alternatively, visit Hveragerði Hot Spring Town — a town built on geothermal activity with a river you can cook eggs in. Walk the Reykjadalur Hot Spring River trail (~3km each way) to reach a natural hot river where you can bathe outdoors.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — choose your favorite restaurant from the trip or try somewhere new. Spend the evening reviewing photos, packing lightly, and doing one final northern lights watch from the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Ölverk Pizza & Brewery in Hveragerði — craft beer brewed with geothermal energy and wood-fired pizza. A fun, relaxed mid-range lunch. ~2,500–4,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for your farewell meal — return to Friðheimar or Lindin Restaurant for a memorable final Icelandic dinner. ~5,000–7,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Reykjadalur hot river hike is approximately 2–3 hours round trip. Bring a swimsuit, towel, and change of clothes in a dry bag. The trail can be icy — crampons recommended. Start no later than 1 PM to return before dark.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Take a short walk around your accommodation area for last views of the Icelandic landscape. Pack and check out. Drive toward Keflavik Airport (~1–1.5 hours from the Golden Circle).
day_by_day.afternoon: If your flight departs in the afternoon or evening, stop at the Reykjanes Peninsula en route to the airport. Visit the Gunnuhver Hot Springs — Iceland's largest hot spring area with dramatic steam vents and mud pools. Free access. Also visit the Reykjanes Lighthouse — the oldest lighthouse in Iceland, perched on dramatic coastal cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Return rental car at Keflavik Airport. Allow 2+ hours before departure for fuel top-up, car return, check-in, and security. Browse duty-free for Icelandic souvenirs: Brennivín schnapps, Nói Síríus chocolate, and Icelandic wool (lopapeysa) sweaters.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor the skyr, rye bread, and smoked salmon one last time.
meals.lunch: Café at Gunnuhver area or grab a meal at Keflavik Airport's mid-range restaurants (Fiskmarkaðurinn or airport café).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on-board flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Return rental car with a full tank — petrol stations at the airport are expensive. Keep a small amount of ISK for parking or airport snacks. Duty-free at Keflavik is excellent and often cheaper than city shops — stock up on Icelandic spirits and chocolate as gifts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Golden Circle & Southern Highlands, Iceland Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the aurora borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover to maximize your viewing experience, often venturing to remote highland locations.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars. Booking the Comfort package includes access to the lagoon, a silica mud mask, and an algae mask for a full rejuvenating experience.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic hot spring sits amid bubbling geysers and steaming vents in a stunning rural landscape, offering a more intimate and local experience.

experiences.name: Skyr Tasting & Icelandic Food Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's culinary scene on a guided food tour sampling traditional Icelandic delicacies including skyr (Icelandic yogurt), lamb soup (kjötsúpa), smoked Arctic char, rye bread baked in geothermal ground, and Brennivín schnapps. Learn about Viking-age food traditions and modern New Nordic cuisine.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike
experiences.description: Trek through the surreal rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains of the Fjallabak Nature Reserve and reward yourself with a soak in the natural geothermal hot spring at Landmannalaugar. The hike offers dramatic lava fields, obsidian rocks, and steaming fumaroles, culminating in a blissful natural hot pool surrounded by mountains.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing at Keflavík International Airport, clear customs and collect luggage. Meet your pre-arranged private luxury transfer driver. Stop en route at the iconic Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa for a late-afternoon soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages and the premium Lava Restaurant dining experience within the lagoon complex. Pre-book the Retreat Spa package for the full luxury immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Continue the scenic 90-minute private transfer through lava fields and volcanic landscapes to your boutique stay in the Golden Circle & Southern Highlands. Check in, settle into your suite, and enjoy a welcome drink by the fireplace. Step outside briefly to scan the night sky — January darkness offers prime Northern Lights viewing conditions directly from the property.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Light bites at Keflavík Airport's Aurora Lounge or on arrival
meals.dinner: Lava Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon — enjoy the tasting menu featuring Icelandic langoustine, Arctic char, and locally foraged ingredients paired with Icelandic craft beer or Scandinavian wines

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa well in advance — January slots fill quickly. Ensure your private transfer is confirmed before departure. Pack a warm layer in carry-on for the outdoor lagoon experience in winter temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and enjoy a lavish breakfast at your boutique hotel. Begin a private guided Golden Circle tour — start at Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá canyon rift in the crisp January morning light (limited daylight hours, roughly 9:00–16:00 in January) and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament, the Alþingi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the spectacular Geysir Geothermal Area to witness Strokkur erupting every 5–10 minutes, shooting boiling water 30 meters into the air. Then proceed to the majestic Gullfoss Waterfall — Iceland's most iconic cascade — partially frozen and dramatically lit in winter. Enjoy the raw power of the falls with far fewer crowds than summer.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel as darkness falls (around 16:00). After freshening up, join a Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — your expert guide will use aurora forecasting apps and drive deep into the wilderness away from all light pollution for the best possible viewing conditions. Wrap up in provided blankets and thermals for a magical sky-gazing experience.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at the boutique hotel — skyr, smoked salmon, rye bread, lamb sausage, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch prepared by the hotel, enjoyed at Gullfoss viewpoint with thermos coffee and Icelandic hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Return to the hotel for a private chef dinner or visit a nearby premium local restaurant featuring slow-roasted Icelandic lamb and root vegetable stew

day_by_day.notes: January sunrise is around 11:00 and sunset around 15:30 — plan all outdoor sightseeing within this window. The Northern Lights Hunt typically runs 20:00–23:00. Dress in thermal base layers, mid-layer fleece, and a waterproof outer shell.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely late breakfast at the hotel, then embark on a private guided tour toward the Haukadalur geothermal valley. Visit lesser-known steaming hot spring vents and fumaroles in the area for an intimate geothermal experience away from the main tourist crowds. Your guide will explain Iceland's volcanic geology in fascinating detail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating back to 1891, naturally heated to a constant 38–40°C. Soak in the rustic, naturally formed pool surrounded by steaming geothermal vents, bubbling hot springs, and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. The intimate setting and authentic Icelandic atmosphere make this a far more personal experience than larger commercial spas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique hotel as darkness falls. Enjoy a private stargazing and Northern Lights vigil on the hotel terrace with a dedicated aurora monitor service. Sip on Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps) and warm mulled wine while waiting for the aurora to dance overhead. If conditions are favorable, the hotel staff will alert you immediately.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast with Icelandic pastries, smoked fish platter, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a local restaurant in Flúðir near the Secret Lagoon — try the traditional Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) and freshly baked rye bread
meals.dinner: Private in-room or dining room dinner at the boutique hotel — chef's tasting menu with Icelandic ingredients, paired with a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is significantly less commercialized than the Blue Lagoon — bring your own luxury toiletries for the changing rooms. January evenings are ideal for Northern Lights if cloud cover is minimal. Check aurora forecast (Vedur.is) each morning.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast followed by a private guided drive south toward the stunning South Coast. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's most unique falls where you can walk behind the cascading curtain of water (may be icy in January — guide will assess safety). The frozen surroundings and ice formations create an otherworldly winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall, one of Iceland's largest and most dramatic cascades. Climb the staircase alongside the falls for panoramic views across the black sand plains toward the sea. Afterward, visit the nearby Skógar Folk Museum to explore Iceland's heritage and traditional turf houses. Continue to the black sand beaches of Reynisfjara — dramatic basalt column formations and roaring Atlantic waves (exercise extreme caution near the waves in winter).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming town of Vík í Mýrdal before heading back north. Stop at a premium local restaurant in Vík for dinner before returning to the hotel. Keep aurora alerts active for the drive back — the South Coast road offers spectacular dark-sky conditions.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet boxed lunch from the hotel, enjoyed with a thermos of soup at Skógafoss
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sudur-Vík Restaurant in Vík — excellent lamb fillet, pan-seared Arctic char, and local seafood dishes in a cozy, upscale setting

day_by_day.notes: January road conditions on Route 1 (Ring Road) can be icy — your private driver will have a 4WD vehicle with studded tires. Walking behind Seljalandsfoss may be closed due to ice — confirm with guide on the day. Reynisfjara sneaker waves are extremely dangerous; never turn your back to the ocean.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Take a private yoga or wellness session if offered by the boutique property, or simply relax in the hotel's hot tub or private geothermal pool. Use the morning to review photos, recharge, and prepare for the next few days of exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided excursion to Kerið Volcanic Crater Lake — a stunning 3,000-year-old explosion crater with vivid red, black, and ochre volcanic rock surrounding a deep teal lake. Walk the full rim of the crater for 360-degree views. Afterward, visit the nearby Skálholt Cathedral, one of Iceland's most historically significant religious sites and former medieval bishopric.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — second dedicated aurora hunt of the trip with a different route into the highlands. Your guide will target areas with the clearest skies based on real-time meteorological and aurora activity data. Hot drinks and snacks provided on the tour.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — fresh waffles with Icelandic cream and crowberry jam, smoked lamb, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or a nearby café — open-faced smoked salmon sandwiches and skyr parfait
meals.dinner: Return to the hotel for a premium dinner — request the chef's special featuring slow-cooked reindeer or Icelandic beef tenderloin

day_by_day.notes: Kerið is a quick 30-minute drive from most Golden Circle accommodations. The Super Jeep Northern Lights tour typically covers 100–200km searching for clear skies — dress extremely warmly as temperatures can drop to -10°C or below.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided snowmobile or glacier hike excursion on Langjökull Glacier — Iceland's second-largest ice cap and one of the most accessible glaciers in winter. Drive through dramatic highland terrain to the glacier edge and don crampons and safety gear for a guided walk across the ancient blue ice. Optional: enter the man-made ice tunnel inside the glacier for a truly unique experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the glacier and stop at Húsafell, a small highland oasis with a private geothermal pool. Enjoy a private soak in the Húsafell Canyon Baths or the Krauma Geothermal Baths — fed by the powerful Deildartunguhver hot spring (Europe's most powerful hot spring) with five naturally heated pools and a cold plunge. This is a deeply relaxing, premium geothermal experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique hotel for a quiet evening. Enjoy dinner at the hotel and spend the evening on the terrace with a glass of Icelandic gin watching for aurora activity. January is statistically one of the best months for Northern Lights sightings in Iceland.

meals.breakfast: High-energy hotel breakfast before the glacier excursion — porridge, eggs, smoked meats, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Warm soup and fresh bread at the Krauma Geothermal Baths café, overlooking the steaming Deildartunguhver spring
meals.dinner: Hotel dinner — ask for the Icelandic lamb rack with roasted root vegetables and red wine jus, paired with a Burgundy or premium New Zealand Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Glacier excursions require sturdy waterproof boots — rental equipment is available on-site. Krauma Geothermal Baths should be pre-booked. The drive to Langjökull from the Golden Circle area is approximately 1.5 hours — depart by 08:30 to maximize daylight.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Reykjavik — private luxury transfer to the capital (approximately 60–90 minutes). Begin with the Skyr Tasting & Icelandic Food Walking Tour through Reykjavik's culinary scene. Sample traditional Icelandic delicacies including skyr, hákarl (fermented shark), kleinur pastries, lamb pâté, and locally brewed craft beers and spirits. Your guide will share fascinating stories about Icelandic food culture and history.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the food tour, explore Reykjavik's highlights privately — visit Hallgrímskirkja Church for panoramic city views from the tower, stroll along the Laugavegur shopping street for premium Icelandic design and woolens (pick up a luxury lopapeysa sweater), and visit the Harpa Concert Hall for its stunning geometric glass architecture overlooking the harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Reykjavik's finest restaurants before returning to the hotel. Reykjavik's fine dining scene is world-class — this is the perfect evening for an exceptional multi-course tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure to Reykjavik
meals.lunch: Covered by the Icelandic Food Walking Tour — multiple tastings across Reykjavik's best food spots
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant (Iceland's premier New Nordic fine dining, Michelin-recognized) — seasonal tasting menu showcasing foraged Icelandic ingredients, fermented produce, and pristine local proteins with exceptional wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Dill Restaurant well in advance — it is one of the most sought-after reservations in Iceland. The food walking tour typically lasts 3 hours. Laugavegur shops close around 18:00 in winter. Arrange private transfer back to the hotel after dinner (approximately 21:00).

day_by_day.morning: Recovery and relaxation morning at the boutique hotel. Enjoy an extended breakfast, then arrange a private in-hotel spa treatment if available — massage, hot stone therapy, or a geothermal facial using Icelandic volcanic mineral products. Alternatively, take a peaceful walk in the snow-covered landscape surrounding the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour to the Landmannalaugar Hot Spring area — one of Iceland's most extraordinary highland destinations. Trek through the surreal rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains of the Fjallabak Nature Reserve (note: full highland access may be limited in deep January — your guide will assess conditions and offer the best accessible route). Reward yourself with a soak in the natural geothermal hot spring pool at the end of the hike, where hot and cold streams mix to create perfect bathing temperatures amid the snow.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a celebratory mid-trip dinner. Toast to the journey so far with a bottle of Champagne and a specially prepared meal by the hotel chef. Spend the late evening aurora watching from the comfort of the hotel's outdoor hot tub.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast with fresh pastries, Icelandic cheese board, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch from the hotel enjoyed at the Landmannalaugar hut — warm soup from a thermos, artisan sandwiches, and energy snacks
meals.dinner: Premium hotel dinner — request a special menu for the occasion, featuring Icelandic lobster (langoustine) bisque, pan-seared ptarmigan, and a dark chocolate and skyr dessert

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar in January requires a super jeep with experienced highland driving expertise — standard vehicles cannot access this area in winter. The geothermal pool here is completely natural and free to use. Bring a dry bag for your towel and change of clothes. Water temperature is approximately 36–40°C.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided whale watching and puffin tour departure from Reykjavik's Old Harbour (approximately 90-minute transfer). January is an excellent month for humpback whale sightings in Faxaflói Bay. Board a premium small-group whale watching vessel with heated indoor cabin, complimentary hot drinks, and expert marine biologist guide. Spot humpback whales, minke whales, and dolphins in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik harbour and explore the Grandi district — Reykjavik's creative waterfront quarter with artisan boutiques, the excellent Saga Museum, and the Marshall House contemporary art gallery. Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) for an immersive underground archaeological experience exploring the original Viking settlement of Reykjavik.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at Sky Bar or a rooftop venue in Reykjavik before a second premium dinner in the city. Return to the boutique hotel via private transfer after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at Matur og Drykkur in Reykjavik's Grandi district — innovative traditional Icelandic recipes including cod head, salted lamb, and hákarl reimagined in a fine dining context
meals.dinner: Ox Restaurant at Grillmarkadurinn (The Grill Market) — premium Icelandic beef, lamb, and seafood over volcanic stone grill, with an extensive Icelandic craft beer and wine list

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching tours in January have an approximately 80% success rate for sightings. Dress in extreme warmth — the open sea in January is bitterly cold. Pre-book the whale watching tour with a premium operator such as Elding or Special Tours. Return transfer to hotel after dinner approximately 22:00.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided ice cave exploration on Vatnajökull Glacier — Iceland's largest glacier and Europe's biggest ice cap. Depart early for the approximately 3-hour drive east toward Skaftafell. Enter a naturally formed crystal-blue ice cave deep within the glacier with your certified glacier guide. The ice caves are only safely accessible in winter (November–March) and offer an absolutely breathtaking display of blue, black, and white ice formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the ice cave tour, visit Skaftafell Nature Reserve within Vatnajökull National Park. Walk to Svartifoss Waterfall — the 'Black Falls' — framed by dramatic dark basalt columns that inspired the design of Hallgrímskirkja Church. The short hike through snow-dusted birch forest is magical in January light.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a premium overnight accommodation near Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (arrange a one-night luxury stay at Fosshotel Glacier Lagoon or similar) to be positioned for an extraordinary sunrise experience the following morning. Dinner at the hotel restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the long drive east
meals.lunch: Warm lunch at Skaftafell Visitor Centre café or a packed gourmet lunch from the hotel
meals.dinner: Dinner at Fosshotel Glacier Lagoon restaurant — locally sourced lamb, glacial river trout, and Icelandic root vegetable dishes

day_by_day.notes: Ice cave tours must be booked with certified guides only — Local Guide of Vatnajökull or Icelandic Mountain Guides are recommended. The drive to Vatnajökull from the Golden Circle is approximately 3–3.5 hours each way — this is best done as an overnight excursion. Helmet and crampons are provided by the tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for the extraordinary experience of Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon at sunrise. Watch as enormous blue icebergs calved from Breiðamerkurjökull Glacier float silently across the lagoon in the first light of day. Walk to Diamond Beach — the black sand shore where translucent ice chunks wash up like scattered diamonds. This is one of Iceland's most iconic and unforgettable landscapes, especially in the golden January light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the scenic drive back west along the Ring Road. Stop at Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon — a stunning 2km-long, 100-meter-deep canyon carved by glacial meltwater, with dramatic twisted rock formations and a crystal-clear river. Continue west and stop at the Lava Centre in Hvolsvöllur — an immersive, high-tech exhibition about Iceland's volcanic activity, earthquakes, and geological history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your boutique hotel in the Golden Circle & Southern Highlands. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a long soak in the hotel's private hot tub or geothermal pool, followed by a quiet dinner and aurora watching from the property.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Fosshotel before sunrise departure to the lagoon
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch enjoyed at Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon viewpoint
meals.dinner: Welcome-back dinner at the boutique hotel — comfort Icelandic cuisine featuring braised short rib, wild mushroom risotto with Icelandic herbs, and a warm skyr cheesecake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón at sunrise in January (around 10:30–11:00) is exceptionally beautiful — arrive by 10:00 for the full experience. The lagoon boat tours do not operate in January but the shoreline walk is equally spectacular. Drive time from Jökulsárlón back to the Golden Circle is approximately 4 hours — depart by 13:00.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated relaxation and wellness morning at the hotel. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and spend the morning in the hotel's wellness facilities. If the property has a private geothermal pool, spend at least an hour soaking while watching the snow-covered Icelandic landscape. Optional: arrange a private guided horse riding tour on Icelandic horses through the snowy countryside — these small, sturdy horses are unique to Iceland and offer a magical winter riding experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final visit to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) for a farewell soak — this time with more leisure and no agenda. Spend 2–3 hours in the naturally heated pool, watching the steam rise against the winter sky and the small geyser erupt beside you. Treat yourself to a post-soak massage at a nearby spa if available.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — a dedicated farewell aurora excursion. Your guide will pull out all the stops for the last night, driving to the darkest, clearest locations available. Celebrate with a glass of Champagne under the stars if the aurora appears. Return to the hotel for a farewell nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final full breakfast at the hotel — order everything on the menu
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the Secret Lagoon in Flúðir
meals.dinner: Premium farewell dinner at the hotel — request a special tasting menu from the chef, featuring the best of Icelandic ingredients: langoustine, lamb, Arctic char, and skyr desserts, paired with a premium Champagne or fine wine

day_by_day.notes: Pack bags and prepare for departure the following morning. Leave out only what you need for the final night. Tip your hotel staff, guides, and drivers generously — Icelandic hospitality is exceptional. Confirm your airport transfer for Day 13.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland — enjoy a last leisurely breakfast at the boutique hotel. Take a slow walk around the property grounds in the morning twilight (sunrise around 11:00 in late January) and absorb the silence of the Icelandic winter landscape one final time. Exchange contact details with hotel staff and guides who made the trip exceptional.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer departs toward Keflavík International Airport (approximately 60–90 minutes from the Golden Circle). En route, make one final stop at the Blue Lagoon if your flight timing allows — book the premium Retreat Spa for a final 2-hour soak before heading to the airport. The Blue Lagoon is conveniently located just 20 minutes from Keflavík Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Check in at Keflavík Airport. Access the premium Saga Lounge or your airline's business class lounge for pre-flight refreshments. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of Northern Lights, geothermal wonders, glaciers, ice caves, and world-class Icelandic cuisine. Depart Iceland with memories to last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor every bite
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant for a final Icelandic meal, or premium dining at Keflavík Airport's Saga Lounge
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon entry on departure day must be timed carefully — allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight departs (check-in, security, and boarding). Most international flights from Keflavík depart in the afternoon or evening, making a final Blue Lagoon stop very feasible. Confirm all luggage storage arrangements and ensure valuables are in carry-on. Iceland's departure tax is included in most international ticket prices.
